newsitem.title: BELGIUM: OLO/Bund spread at bottom of range, seen wider.
newsitem.headline: OLO/Bund spread at bottom of range, seen wider.

text.p: Belgian linear bond futures staged a rebound on Wednesday after the FOMC's decision to leave rates unchanged, but the undertone remained bearish.
Dealers said that attention would now switch back to economic data, which will be inspected with a fine-tooth comb for any signs of inflation.
"All the downward potential linked to a rate hike is still there. The question is now when it will come," one dealer said.
OLO futures were up 34 bp at 121.50, the 2007 OLO yield stood at 5.85%. The OLO/Bund spread narrowed to seven bps over Bunds from nine, at the bottom of its recent range.
"At this level, it makes more sense to buy Bunds against Belgium. The potential for further narrowing is very small," one dealer said, adding he expected a bout of profittaking.
The Belgian Treasury announced that it will auction the January 2000 OLO 27 and the March 2007 OLO 26 at its monthly auction on Monday, May 26.
Dealers said that after Tuesday's small exchange auction, volume at the monthly auction could be above average.
Very short money rates remained well above the central rate, with one-week repos at 3.14/18 percent.
-- Geert De Clercq, Brussels Newsroom +32 2 287 6813, Fax +32 2 230 7710
